cells.tense: Right now you are standing in the open before anything has been decided.
cells.act: let yourself want it, plainly, to yourself
cells.ask: Pick the direction whose loss would sting most, keep it quietly in your own head for a day, and put your hours there — just the moving, no verdict on whether it is right.
cells.core:
You are moving toward something, and you have not yet narrowed what it is — not from confusion, but because nothing has been closed off. The road is open and you are on it, and the not-knowing is carrying you rather than slowing you. Most people lose this early. You have it now, and it is doing real work.

What comes next is to want one direction plainly, in your own head, and steer by it for a day. There is a particular thing you have not quite said to yourself, because saying it would shut other doors — and shutting them is what makes motion possible. Pick it, hold it quietly, and give it a day of your hours. You are not promising forever. You are letting one direction hold the push, so the energy has somewhere to go.
cells.sheetLine: The not-knowing is carrying you. Want one direction anyway.
cells.verb: Holding everything open before choosing what to become
cells.place: On the road toward a goal, still in motion

cells.tense: You will keep every possibility open, and your hands stay clean of any one of them.
cells.act: put your own name on what is already yours
cells.ask: Choose something you keep describing to yourself instead of doing, do it today with nobody watching, then write your name on it — no announcement, no rehearsal, no reasoning.
cells.core:
There is a way this goes wrong. You keep every option open because closing one feels like a loss, and holding them all becomes the work. From outside it looks like you are still deciding. From inside you are hovering, and the motion keeps missing anything solid. Potential that does not land stops being potential and turns into a kind of waiting.

What breaks it is smaller than deciding everything. This week, take something you keep talking about and just do it, without an audience and without explaining yourself afterward. Not the biggest one — a small one, done with your own hands. What you are is not a set of options; it is a way of moving, and it shows most clearly when you quit hovering and move. It gets easier after that.

cells.tense: Something you were once open to has gone tight, and you are still making things from there.
cells.act: look at the same thing longer, until it shows you more
cells.ask: Take a goal you are pushing toward and sit with it ten minutes past what feels useful — what it sits beside, what it costs — deciding nothing yet.
cells.core:
The drive is still yours, and here it runs small. You start something and it comes out tight, guarded, already braced for a hit. The ease of beginning without a plan has thinned, and you are building from a narrow place you did not choose. This is not a lack of wanting more. It is a lack of room.

Pushing harder will not open it. Step back and take in the whole arrangement you are standing inside — what this goal sits beside, what it costs, what else it touches. From that distance, desire comes back without being forced. Look at it longer than feels productive. You are not hunting a verdict. You are looking for what you have not yet seen.
cells.sheetLine: You are making things from behind a wall. Look longer than feels useful.

cells.tense: You are moving toward something, and the hand on the wheel is not being counted as yours.
cells.act: let the path show itself instead of forcing clarity
cells.ask: Let one step of a goal you are pushing toward be enough — no map of the whole road, no forcing the picture — and afterward notice you are the one who moved.
cells.core:
You are already steering, and you do not count it as steering. Choices get made — this way, not that — and they feel like reactions to what is nearby, not like anything you wrote. The options are there. You are walking through some of them. You just do not see the walking as yours.

A bigger decision is not the fix. A smaller one is. Let one step of a goal you are pushing toward be enough, letting the path show itself instead of forcing the whole picture. You are already moving through uncertainty, and moving through it is yours — you do not need to know where it ends to know you are the one who went. Notice the hand on the wheel after the step, not before.
